messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in prefill OOMs on gpu-pool-us-west-2. metric: prefill_container_restarts ↑, 5xx_rate ↑. paging oncall_ryan :rotating_light:

oncall_ryan: I’m on it. grabbing logs and checking affected nodes.

ops_nadia: seeing repeated 'CUDA out of memory' in container logs for model=redwood-13b-ctx64k. sample:
```
E tensorflow: CUDA error: out of memory
  at serve/runtime/prefill.cc:line 412
  kv_cache_alloc failed size=1.2G
```

oncall_ryan: OOMs clustered on node gpu-12.us-west-2, containers keep restarting (~3/min). I'm going to cordon+drain to stop noisy neighbor.

ops_nadia: ack. starting drain: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

prod-support-ana: CustomerImpact: 3 customers reported increased 5xxs in last 8m, highest affected app is acme-chat (tenant-acme-001). Preparing customer update.

eng-runtime-sam: joining. probable trigger: very long prefill windows from a small set of requests (single request with ~120k tokens of prompt expansion). Our prefetch matcher attempted full KV allocation -> fragmentation and eventual OOM.

eng-runtime-sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefill for long-window models (short-circuit prefetch), 2) evict large KV allocations proactively, 3) route >X token requests to coldmodel tier.

oncall_ryan: apply 1 and 3 now. Nadia, can you push config change to mutate prefill policy for model redwood-13b-ctx64k?

ops_nadia: applying patch to configmap: `kubectl patch configmap/prefill-policy -p '{"data":{"redwood-13b-ctx64k":"disable_prefill=true;route_to_cold=true;max_prefill_tokens=8192"}}'`

ops_nadia: rolling restart of runtime pods in pool now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-gpu-pool-us-west-2`

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled in 30m. tag @eng-runtime for follow-ups.

prod-support-ana: Drafting customer blurb: "We detected GPU memory errors impacting inference for long-context requests. We’ve applied a temporary routing policy to protect stability; performance for long-context requests may be degraded while we mitigate. We're following up with a timeline." Thoughts?

cust-success-lee: send to acme-chat escalation channel, mention potential token-trimming workaround on their side and offer to help craft prompt-shortening rules.

eng-runtime-sam: logs show immediate drop in OOM spikes after policy applied. sample from metrics: prefill_ooms 120->6 in 5m, container_restarts 18->2.

oncall_ryan: confirming. I see node drained and restarted pods on alternate nodes. No further cuda driver resets but a few containers hit prefill timeouts and returned 429-like errors during routing.

ops_nadia: temporarily enabled per-tenant prefill caps for the largest tenants as an extra throttle. config: `TENANT_PREFILL_CAPS: {"tenant-acme-001":4096}`

eng-runtime-sam: plan for next 24h: 1) persistent fix: patch allocator to pre-reserve KV arenas to avoid fragmentation; 2) improve prefill admission gating by token-count; 3) add coldmodel routing for >32k tokens; 4) add regression alert to detect single-request token explosion.

prod-support-ana: customer update posted to status page and acme-chat team notified.

cust-success-lee: acme replied: appreciated, will try trimming prompts. requesting ETA for full fix.

eng-runtime-sam: ETA for code fix ~48-72h, can propose a safer hotpatch for allocator in ~12-24h.

oncall_ryan: passing to night oncall with notes. will keep watch on escalations.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (prefill disabled for redwood-13b-ctx64k; tenant caps enabled), customer notifications posted. Severity downgraded to SEV-3.

oncall_ryan: closing realtime mitigation. opened a follow-up engineering ticket (ENG-PR-XXXX) for allocator patch + routing improvements. leaving the drain state until autoscaler stabilizes.

ops_nadia: final logs attached in incident tracker. no further restarts observed for 20m.

eng-runtime-sam: thanks everyone. will post postmortem draft tomorrow. :thumbsup:
